body: Hawaiian Airlines is concentrating its cabin investment on its fleet of 24 Airbus A330-200s, which will be reconfigured with new interiors and four cabin types by 2028. The front cabin will become the Leihoku Suites, with 22 lie-flat suites in a 1-2-1 layout with sliding doors, replacing today's 18 lie-flat seats in a 2-2-2 layout, each with a 19-inch 4K screen, chef-designed dining with wine pairings, hotel-quality bedding, Starlink WiFi for Atmos Rewards members and a dedicated check-in and concierge service in Honolulu and Seattle. The second cabin, Premium Reserve, offers 38 inches of seat pitch and a 16-inch OLED touchscreen, while economy passengers will get a new 13-inch 4K OLED touchscreen.

The reconfiguration changes the A330 layout from 18 business class seats and 260 economy seats, of which 68 are Premium Class, to 22 business class seats, 28 premium economy seats and 204 economy seats, of which 48 are Premium Class. Hawaiian's chief executive said the retrofit will remove four economy seats and replace them with 12 higher-class seats, and that earning more from the front of the aircraft takes pressure off fares at the back. A new 200-guest lounge in Honolulu's Terminal 1 is also part of the refresh and is set to open in early 2028.

Hawaiian's narrowbody fleet is not getting the same treatment. Its 19 Boeing 717s, which serve interisland routes, are due to retire and be replaced by mid-aged Boeing 737-800s transferred from Alaska starting in 2028, with the phase-out set to begin that year; Hawaiian has so far received one 737-800 from Alaska. The future of its 18 Airbus A321neos, the fleet's most modern aircraft at an average age of just seven years, remains undetermined: Alaska has said the fleet will either double in size or be phased out entirely, with no final decision expected until around 2027-2028, so investing in new interiors for them now would be risky.
en.summary: Hawaiian is overhauling the cabins of its 24 Airbus A330-200s with Leihoku Suites and four cabin types by 2028, while its 717s head for retirement and its A321neos await a fleet decision.
en.title: Hawaiian overhauls premium experience on 24 Airbus A330s, leaves narrowbodies untouched

body: 夏威夷航空把客艙投資集中在24架空中巴士A330-200機隊，預定2028年前完成新客艙改裝、改為4種艙等。前艙將改為Leihoku套房，以1-2-1配置提供22個全平躺套房並附拉門，取代現有2-2-2配置的18個平躺座位，每個套房配備19吋4K螢幕、主廚設計餐點與佐餐酒、飯店等級寢具、Atmos Rewards會員專用的Starlink無線網路，以及檀香山與西雅圖的專屬報到與禮賓服務。第二艙Premium Reserve提供38吋座椅間距與16吋OLED觸控螢幕，經濟艙旅客則可使用全新13吋4K OLED觸控螢幕。
改裝後A330的配置將從商務艙18座、經濟艙260座（其中68座為Premium Class），改為商務艙22座、豪華經濟艙28座、經濟艙204座（其中48座為Premium Class）。夏威夷航空執行長表示，改裝將減少4個經濟艙座位、換成12個高階艙位座位，前艙收入增加有助減輕後艙票價壓力。改裝計畫還包括檀香山第一航廈一座可容納200位旅客的新貴賓室，預定2028年初啟用。

夏威夷航空的窄體機隊則不在這波改裝範圍內。19架波音717執飛島際航線，即將退役並自2028年起由阿拉斯加航空轉入的中齡波音737-800取代，汰換預定2028年展開，夏威夷航空目前已接收1架737-800。至於機隊中最新的18架空中巴士A321neo，平均機齡僅7年，未來仍未定：阿拉斯加航空表示該機隊不是擴大一倍、就是全面汰除，最終決定預計要到2027至2028年前後才會出爐，因此現階段投入新客艙並不划算。
zh.summary: 夏威夷航空將為24架A330-200換上Leihoku套房與4種艙等、2028年前完成，717機隊走向退役，A321neo的去留則待阿拉斯加航空決定。
zh.title: 夏威夷航空大改24架A330高階客艙，窄體機隊暫不動
